title: Gujarat's Swaminarayan
hook: a scripture made of questions asked out loud in a village courtyard

segments.voice: Yesterday, Gujarat's Swaminarayan: Nilkanth became Sahajanand Swami under Ramanand, and the mantra Swaminarayan became his name.

Evening in a village in Gujarat. A courtyard, a raised seat, a crowd on the ground: farmers, merchants, robed sadhus, children at the edges. The teacher on the seat is Swaminarayan, and he invites questions. Someone asks a hard one. Why does the mind keep running back to the same old cravings, even after years of devotion? He answers. Someone pushes back. He answers again. And off to one side, a few senior sadhus listen very closely, because they're going to write this down. Today, a holy book that began as a conversation.
screen: `A COURTYARD AT EVENING.` → `SOMEONE ASKS A HARD ONE.` → `SOMEONE WRITES IT DOWN.`

segments.voice: The book is the Vachanamrut. Followers hear the title as vachan, words, and amrut, the nectar of immortality: nectar in the form of words. They hold it as scripture, his own teaching, gathered from talks in Gadhada and other villages, each headed with the place, the setting, even what he was wearing that evening. First, its shape. It arrives as dialogue. A devotee asks, Swaminarayan answers, and sometimes he turns it around and asks the room, waiting to see who can answer. Learning happens in public, and sometimes the room has no answer to give. Then, the content. The questions are practical. How do you know if your devotion is real? What do you do with anger toward someone in your own community? Why does a person who has heard good teaching still not change? Kitchen-table questions, treated as worth a scripture. Last, the thread. Running through the answers is what tradition calls ekantik dharma, a whole-hearted life held up by four things together: dharma, doing what's right; knowing the self as distinct from the body; vairagya, detachment; and bhakti, love for God. Not one of them alone. All four lean on each other, like the legs of a cot. So a scripture of questions also trusts the people asking. The answers matter. So does the fact that someone was allowed to ask.
screen: `VACHANAMRUT — NECTAR IN WORDS` · `A SCRIPTURE THAT BEGINS AS DIALOGUE` · `KITCHEN-TABLE QUESTIONS` · `FOUR THINGS HELD TOGETHER`

segments.voice: Give one breath to each leg of the cot: doing what's right, knowing yourself as more than the body, letting go, and love, for one face or, if you pray, for God. Then notice, without judging, which leg feels steady today and which one wobbles, and rest on the whole cot for a few breaths.
Gujarat's Swaminarayan. Today, the Vachanamrut, his teaching kept as questions and answers from evening gatherings. Today's word.
Your line: Gujarat's Swaminarayan. In his courtyard, a hard question was welcome. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: In Swaminarayan mandirs and homes, passages from the Vachanamrut are read aloud and explained at gatherings, and devotees study it together.
